facts: Automatic image annotation is a newly developed technique.
Automatic image annotation is a promising technique.
Automatic image annotation provides semantic image retrieval via text descriptions.
The image contents are labeled with a pre-defined set of keywords.
The pre-defined set of keywords is exploited to represent the image semantics.
A Maximum Entropy Model-based approach to automatic image annotation is proposed.
In the training phase, a basic visual vocabulary is generated at first.
The basic visual vocabulary consists of blob-tokens.
The statistical relationship between the blob-tokens and keywords is modeled by a Maximum Entropy Model.
The Maximum Entropy Model is constructed from the training set of labeled images.
In the annotation phase, for an unlabeled image, the most likely associated keywords are predicted.
The prediction of associated keywords is made in terms of the blob-token set extracted from the given image.
Experiments were carried out on a medium-sized image collection with about 5000 images from Corel Photo CDs.
The annotation performance of the Maximum Entropy Model-based approach outperforms some traditional annotation methods by about 8% in mean precision.
The experimental results show a potential of the Maximum Entropy Model in the task of automatic image annotation.
